content: Telavancin is a medication that may rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to an overgrowth of the bacterium Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or even weeks to months after the treatment has been discontinued. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. While serious allergic reactions to telavancin are rare, they can occur. It is important to note that this is not a comprehensive list of potential side effects. If you are in the United States or Canada and experience side effects, contact your doctor for medical advice. Before using telavancin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Telavancin has the potential to cause a condition that affects the heart's rhythm, known as QT prolongation. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other medications that can also cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can further elevate this risk, especially if you are using certain drugs like diuretics (commonly referred to as water pills) or if you experience conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Telavancin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when absolutely necessary, as it may harm an unborn baby. Consult your doctor for more details, especially regarding the warning section. It is currently unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. It is essential to maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs as well as herbal products, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. Telavancin may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as coagulation tests (e.g., PT/INR/aPTT) and urine protein tests, potentially leading to false test results. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. While using this medication, your doctor may order laboratory or medical tests, such as kidney function tests, to monitor your progress and check for side effects. If you miss a dose of this medication, it is important to contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. For storage instructions, consult the product guidelines and your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in May 2024. It is important to understand that this summary does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
